stations.title: A headache after the festival: fever, headache and neck stiffness in an 18-year-old woman in general practice
stations.desc: In this station the candidate takes a focused headache history from Molly, an 18-year-old university student seen in general practice, and does a focused examination. She came home from a three-day music festival recently. She had a runny nose 3 days ago, and since yesterday evening she has had a worsening, generalised throbbing headache with fever, neck stiffness and photophobia. She has no rash. In Part 2 the candidate first reads her observations, gives an ISBAR handover to the ED, makes the diagnosis and plans emergency management in general practice, including notifying public health. They are then given her CSF and blood results from the hospital, which confirm meningococcal meningitis. They plan definitive treatment, clearance antibiotics for her close contacts through public health, and safety netting for those contacts.
diagnosis: Bacterial meningitis due to Neisseria meningitidis (meningococcal meningitis)
stations.focus: Recognising bacterial meningitis from a fever-and-headache history, giving parenteral antibiotics and arranging emergency transfer from general practice, interpreting CSF, and protecting close contacts of a patient with meningococcal disease

stations.title: A needle in my back? Consent for an urgent lumbar puncture in a 32-year-old woman with headache and fever in the emergency department
stations.desc: In this station the candidate sees Jenny, a 32-year-old stay-at-home mother, in the emergency department. She has had a headache and fever since yesterday, and the ED registrar wants to do an urgent lumbar puncture. The candidate takes a focused history that screens for contraindications to lumbar puncture. They then examine for meningism, rash, papilloedema, focal signs, the source of infection and the skin of her lower back, and obtain informed consent for the lumbar puncture. In Part 2 the candidate reads her observations, bloods and CSF results and diagnoses bacterial meningitis (probably pneumococcal, from a left middle ear infection). They outline the steroid and antibiotic treatment already started, the vancomycin to add, admission, notification and follow-up.
stations.focus: Obtaining informed consent for an urgent lumbar puncture after screening for contraindications, then interpreting CSF and managing bacterial meningitis without delaying antibiotics

stations.title: A wheezy 3-year-old after a cold
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history from the mother of a 3-year-old boy brought to a metropolitan ED with wheeze and breathlessness that came on overnight after 2 days of a cold, then a focused examination. The candidate interprets his observations and a respiratory viral PCR, assesses severity, diagnoses viral-induced (preschool) wheeze, and outlines ED management, spacer teaching and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute wheeze in a preschool child: a BINDS-based paediatric history, excluding anaphylaxis and an inhaled foreign body, grading severity, and managing viral-induced wheeze with spacer teaching

stations.title: Abdominal pain and swelling in a 53-year-old dairy farmer
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 53-year-old dairy farmer in a rural general practice. He has had 1 day of left lower quadrant pain that began suddenly as cramps and is now constant, with severe abdominal distension, early obstipation and late bilious vomiting. He has had diverticulitis before, had colonic polyps removed 5 years ago and never had the surveillance colonoscopy, and his father had colon cancer. The candidate then interprets two sets of observations (getting worse), a urine dipstick and his old colonoscopy report. They recognise probable large bowel obstruction, arrange urgent transfer to hospital, explain the causes of small and large bowel obstruction, and safety-net.
diagnosis: Suspected colorectal cancer or diverticular stricture
stations.focus: Recognising large bowel obstruction from the history and examination, telling it apart from its differentials, and arranging safe, urgent transfer from general practice

stations.title: Abdominal pain, diarrhoea and vomiting in a 69-year-old woman
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 69-year-old woman with sudden diffuse crampy abdominal pain, watery diarrhoea and vomiting after contact with a sick grandchild. The candidate then interprets her observations, bloods, venous gas and ECG, recognises acute gastroenteritis with dehydration and a prerenal acute kidney injury, and manages her fluids, her regular medicines (sick day rules), infection control and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute infectious diarrhoea in an older woman with diabetes: dehydration, AKI and sick day medication rules

stations.title: Abnormal CTG on the birth suite
stations.desc: This station involves a rapid focused history and examination of a woman in induced labour whose CTG has changed, then interpreting the CTG, her observations and a reassessment, managing umbilical cord prolapse with tachysystole and maternal hypotension as a student working with the midwife, and explaining to the woman what is happening.
stations.focus: Intrapartum obstetric emergency: abnormal CTG and cord prolapse in labour

stations.title: Abrupt dry cough and fever in a 34-year-old builder
stations.desc: This station is a focused acute cough history and respiratory examination of Charlie, a 34-year-old builder seen in general practice. He has had an abrupt dry cough with coughing fits for 3 days, with fever, malaise, a sore throat and nasal congestion. A friend has also been coughing, and he did not have the flu vaccine this year. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations and a respiratory PCR swab, diagnoses uncomplicated influenza A and answers his COVID question. They then give supportive care without antibiotics or antivirals, advise him on infection control, vaccination and quitting smoking, and safety-net.
stations.focus: Acute cough: a focused respiratory history and review of systems, then recognising and managing uncomplicated influenza in general practice

stations.title: Aching hands, knees, hips and back in a 56-year-old farmer
stations.desc: This station involves a focused joint pain history and musculoskeletal examination of a 56-year-old farmer in general practice. She has 6 months of gradually worsening mechanical pain in her hands, knees, hips and lower back. In Part 2 the candidate interprets her inflammatory markers, serology, kidney function and hand X-ray, then outlines non-surgical management of osteoarthritis led by exercise and weight loss, and safety-nets.
stations.focus: Polyarticular joint pain: telling osteoarthritis from inflammatory arthritis in the history, examination and results, then evidence-based management of osteoarthritis in general practice

stations.title: Acute chest pain in general practice: cardiovascular examination
stations.desc: This station involves a brief, focused chest pain history and a full cardiovascular examination of a 60-year-old smoker with hypertension and high cholesterol who walks into a general practice with acute chest pain. The candidate then interprets his observations and 12-lead ECG, and outlines the immediate management in general practice, the ambulance transfer for reperfusion and the safety netting.
stations.focus: Cardiovascular examination, then recognising and managing a STEMI in general practice

stations.title: Acutely painful, hot, swollen left knee in a 70-year-old man with diabetes
stations.desc: This station involves a focused joint pain history and examination of a 70-year-old retired engineer who comes to his GP with an acutely painful, hot, swollen left knee. He cannot bear weight. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, a urine dipstick and his most recent practice bloods. They recognise septic arthritis, arrange same-day hospital transfer for joint aspiration before antibiotics, plan the synovial fluid analysis and safety-net.
stations.focus: Acute hot monoarthritis: a focused joint pain history and examination, recognising septic arthritis and arranging aspiration before antibiotics

stations.title: Annual diabetes review in a 57-year-old man: numb toes and an overdue eye check
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and a lower limb examination of a 57-year-old man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes at his annual review. The candidate then interprets his retinal photograph, fasting bloods and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, explains the long-term complications, and plans the annual cycle of care, management of his complications and safety netting in general practice.
diagnosis: Type 2 diabetes with poor glycaemic control
stations.focus: Annual cycle of care in type 2 diabetes: finding and managing microvascular complications (retinopathy, neuropathy and the at-risk foot, nephropathy) and cardiovascular risk in general practice

stations.title: Assault with neck laceration and nasal injury
stations.desc: This station involves a trauma primary survey with immediate management of a neck wound over the external jugular vein, a focused AMPLE history and a nasal examination, then interpreting the reassessment, blood gas, bloods and CT report, and managing and explaining a nasal septal haematoma with safety netting.
stations.focus: Trauma primary survey in the ED: neck and nasal injuries

stations.title: Awful dizzy attacks: episodic vertigo with right ear symptoms in a 55-year-old woman in general practice
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and a focused ear and neurological examination of a 55-year-old woman in general practice who has had two attacks of spinning vertigo, each lasting about 8 hours, over 3 months. She also has fluctuating hearing loss, tinnitus and fullness in her right ear, and she fears a brain tumour. The candidate then interprets her observations and audiology report, diagnoses Ménière's disease, and plans ENT referral, treatment for attacks, lifestyle measures, opportunistic preventive care (sexual health, smoking, cancer screening), safety advice about driving and red flags.
diagnosis: Smoking, unprotected sex and cancer screening (opportunistic)
stations.focus: Telling vertigo from other dizziness by its timing, triggers and ear symptoms, and diagnosing and managing Ménière's disease in general practice

stations.title: Baby not breathing at birth
stations.desc: This station involves leading the first steps of resuscitation of a term baby who is floppy and apnoeic at birth and then, once the neonatal team has taken over, taking a focused history from the midwife, then interpreting the resuscitation record against the ANZCOR SpO2 targets, the cord gas and the blood glucose, outlining post-resuscitation care with doses for this baby, and safety-netting the family.
stations.focus: Neonatal resuscitation of a baby who is not breathing at birth

stations.title: Blackout in the bank queue in a 76-year-old man
stations.desc: In this station the candidate takes a focused history and examination from Frank, a 76-year-old man brought to the ED after a sudden 30-second blackout while standing in a bank queue. The blackout had no warning and followed a few minutes of palpitations, and he recovered quickly and fully. He takes metoprolol and has a slow, regular pulse. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, which include a symptomatic pause, his 12-lead ECG and his blood results. They then recognise complete heart block causing cardiac syncope, manage symptomatic bradycardia in the ED and explain the plan to Frank, who lives alone.
stations.focus: Transient loss of consciousness: separating cardiac syncope from vasovagal syncope and seizure, recognising complete heart block and managing symptomatic bradycardia

stations.title: Boggy uterus after a big baby
stations.desc: This station involves a rapid focused history and examination of a woman bleeding heavily after the birth of a big baby, then interpreting her reassessment and the placenta, managing an atonic postpartum haemorrhage with consented bimanual compression, speaking to her partner, recognising retained placental tissue and safety-netting.
stations.focus: Atonic postpartum haemorrhage on the labour ward

stations.title: Breathless after a mountain bike fall
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 20-year-old man brought to the ED by ambulance after falling onto his left side while mountain biking, now breathless with left pleuritic chest pain and deteriorating. The candidate must recognise a tension pneumothorax clinically and call for decompression without waiting for imaging. They then interpret his observations, bloods with a venous gas and the chest X-ray, justify the diagnosis against the differentials (cardiac tamponade, haemothorax, rib fractures, asthma, PE), and outline ED management and safety netting.
stations.focus: Breathlessness after blunt chest trauma: recognising tension pneumothorax as a clinical diagnosis, decompressing before imaging, and reading the chest X-ray

stations.title: Breathless after lacrosse in a 20-year-old with asthma
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of Terry Wakefield, a 20-year-old university student who presents to a tertiary ED with breathlessness that started while playing lacrosse. He uses only a reliever, takes no preventer and had a cold last week. The candidate then interprets his observations and his lung function tests from a few months ago, grades the severity of the attack, justifies the diagnosis against the differentials, and outlines ED management, discharge planning and safety netting.
diagnosis: Poorly controlled asthma without a preventer
stations.focus: Acute breathlessness in a young man with asthma: eliciting triggers, control and risk of a severe attack, excluding the differentials, grading severity, interpreting spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility, and managing acute severe asthma

stations.title: Breathless lying flat a year after a heart attack
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 69-year-old woman brought to a metropolitan ED with 4 months of worsening breathlessness, orthopnoea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea and ankle swelling a year after an anterior STEMI. The candidate then interprets her observations, ECG, bloods and chest X-ray, diagnoses decompensated biventricular heart failure, and outlines management and safety netting.
stations.focus: Progressive breathlessness: quantifying exercise tolerance, eliciting left and right heart failure symptoms and risk factors, excluding the differentials, and starting heart failure management

stations.title: Breathless on the hills: exertional dyspnoea and a smoker's cough in a retired teacher
stations.desc: This station is a focused dyspnoea history and respiratory examination of Phoebe Hartley, a 65-year-old retired teacher in general practice. She has months of worsening exertional breathlessness, a chronic cough productive of white sputum, wheeze, frequent chest infections and a 50 pack-year smoking history, and she fears heart failure or lung cancer. In Part 2 the candidate interprets her observations, spirometry, chest X-ray and bloods, diagnoses moderate COPD, explains a management plan to her (smoking, diet and alcohol, physical activity and pulmonary rehabilitation, vaccinations, inhalers with spacer technique), and safety-nets with a written action plan, flare-up signs and follow-up that includes an ECG and cardiovascular risk assessment.
stations.focus: Exertional breathlessness in a heavy smoker: a dyspnoea history that screens cardiac, malignant and interstitial causes, then confirming COPD on spirometry and explaining a COPD-X management plan to the patient

stations.title: Breathlessness after a 20 km run in a 20-year-old man
stations.desc: This station is a focused breathlessness history and a full respiratory examination of Sam Jones, a 20-year-old university student seeing his GP. He became short of breath during his first 20 km run and it has now settled. Every examination finding is normal. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, a chest X-ray report and spirometry, all of which are normal. They should conclude that this is physiological exertional breathlessness after an unaccustomed run, explain why pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism, cardiac disease and exercise-induced bronchoconstriction are unlikely or not yet excluded, name the investigations used for breathlessness, say when a V/Q scan is preferred over a CTPA, and safety-net.
stations.focus: A complete, systematic respiratory examination in a well young man with exertional breathlessness, then interpreting normal results, ruling out the dangerous causes and choosing investigations

stations.title: Bright red rectal bleeding in a 42-year-old engineer
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 42-year-old electronics engineer in general practice. He has had 2 days of painless bright red blood on the toilet paper, a feeling of fullness after opening his bowels, years of on-and-off constipation and a low-fibre diet. He is worried about bowel cancer because his father died of cancer. The candidate then interprets a proctoscopy report and blood tests, recognises grade I internal haemorrhoids, and plans conservative treatment, referral for colonoscopy and safety netting.
presentation: Bright red blood on the toilet paper
stations.focus: Rectal bleeding in general practice: telling haemorrhoids apart from the differentials that matter, assessing colorectal cancer risk, and planning conservative treatment and colonoscopy

stations.title: Bumping into things on the left: cranial nerve examination in a 78-year-old man admitted with suspected stroke
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and a cranial nerve examination of a 78-year-old man on the general medicine ward with a suspected stroke, who keeps bumping into things on his left. The candidate then interprets his formal visual fields, MRI brain, ECG and bloods, explains how visual field testing tells a posterior from a middle cerebral artery infarct, and plans stroke unit care, anticoagulation for newly found atrial fibrillation, secondary prevention and driving advice.
diagnosis: Left homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing
stations.focus: Cranial nerve examination and localising a homonymous visual field defect to an arterial territory in posterior circulation stroke

stations.title: Burning chest pain after meals in a 45-year-old basketball coach
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 45-year-old woman in the ED with 4 weeks of burning central chest pain that is worse lying down and after meals, who fears a heart attack because her father died of one. The candidate then interprets her observations, ECG, serial high-sensitivity troponin and bloods, recognises that acute MI is excluded and that she is low risk for ACS, recognises reflux with alarm features, and outlines management, the complications of reflux, and safety netting.
context: Family history of premature coronary disease
diagnosis: Acute MI excluded; low risk for ACS on serial high-sensitivity troponin
stations.focus: Separating reflux from acute coronary syndrome in ED chest pain, and recognising the alarm features that need a gastroscopy

stations.title: Burning chest pain after meals in general practice
stations.desc: This station involves a focused chest pain history and examination of a 54-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and asthma who has had four months of daily burning retrosternal pain after meals. The candidate then interprets his ECG and blood tests, gives a diagnosis and differentials, and outlines GP management of reflux (lifestyle changes, a PPI trial and when to refer for endoscopy) without missing a cardiac cause, then safety-nets.
stations.focus: Chest pain history: telling reflux from cardiac pain, GORD management and when to refer for endoscopy

stations.title: Calf pain in a young woman on the pill
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 26-year-old woman with two days of left calf pain, then interpreting her observations, a compression ultrasound with Doppler and baseline bloods, applying the Wells score, planning anticoagulation and contraception in general practice, and safety-netting.
stations.focus: Unilateral calf pain: VTE risk factor history, Wells score, compression ultrasound and outpatient DVT management

stations.title: Central chest pain in a 50-year-old man
stations.desc: This station involves a focused chest pain history and examination of a 50-year-old man brought to the ED by ambulance, who becomes bradycardic and hypotensive during the history. The candidate then interprets his observations, 12-lead ECG and bloods, recognises an inferior STEMI, and outlines reperfusion, immediate management, secondary prevention and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute chest pain: a focused history, recognising an inferior STEMI on the ECG, and immediate reperfusion and secondary prevention

stations.title: Chest flutters in a 69-year-old teacher
stations.desc: This station is a focused palpitations history and cardiovascular examination of Philip Miller, a 69-year-old history teacher. He presents to a rural emergency department with 40 minutes of sudden, racing ‘chest flutters’, light-headedness and central chest tightness. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, 12-lead ECG and blood results. They should diagnose new-onset atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response that started less than 48 hours ago in a haemodynamically stable patient, then outline rate control, stroke risk and anticoagulation, the place of cardioversion and the disposition. Finally they answer his fear of a heart attack, including the complications of AF and safety netting.
diagnosis: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (new onset, under 48 hours)
stations.focus: Palpitations: a structured history with cluster questions, then recognising and managing new-onset atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response

stations.title: Chest pain and breathlessness while walking the dog in a 70-year-old man
stations.desc: This station involves a focused chest pain history and examination of a 70-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension and COPD who is in the ED with 2 hours of central chest pressure and breathlessness. The candidate then interprets his observations, 12-lead ECG, bloods and chest X-ray, recognises an NSTEMI, explains how the types of acute coronary syndrome are told apart, and outlines management and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute chest pain: a focused cardiovascular history with cluster questions, recognising an NSTEMI on ECG and serial troponin, and telling apart STEMI, NSTEMI and unstable angina

stations.title: Chest pain, fever and breathlessness after a bereavement
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of an acutely unwell older woman with chest pain, fever and breathlessness after a bereavement, then interpreting her observations, ECG, bloods and chest X-ray, risk stratifying with CURB-65 and PERC, placing Takotsubo cardiomyopathy as a differential, and outlining management and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute chest pain and breathlessness: risk stratifying PE, pneumonia and Takotsubo

stations.title: Chest pressure radiating to the arm and jaw in a regional emergency department
stations.desc: This station involves a focused chest pain history and examination of a 64-year-old pizza shop manager brought by ambulance to a regional ED without a cardiac catheter laboratory. His pain returns during the history. The candidate then interprets his observations, 12-lead ECG, bloods and chest X-ray, recognises an anterior (anterolateral) STEMI, and outlines reperfusion when timely PCI is not available, along with immediate management and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute chest pain: a focused history, reading an anterior STEMI systematically, and choosing reperfusion in a regional hospital without PCI

stations.title: Chronic diarrhoea in a 21-year-old university student
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 21-year-old university student in general practice with 12 weeks of pale, floating loose stools, fatigue, weight loss and bloating. He mentions an itchy rash on both knees only if asked, and he has a family history of type 1 diabetes and thyroid disease. The candidate then interprets a photograph of the rash, his blood tests and his coeliac serology, recognises coeliac disease with dermatitis herpetiformis and iron and folate deficiency, and plans confirmation, nutritional assessment, family screening and safety netting.
stations.focus: Chronic diarrhoea in a young adult: excluding red flags, finding the rash, and working up coeliac disease

stations.title: Colicky abdominal pain and vomiting in a 45-year-old hairdresser
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 45-year-old woman in a rural ED with 3 days of colicky periumbilical pain, bilious vomiting, no stool or flatus, and previous caesarean sections and appendicectomy. The candidate then interprets her observations, bloods, venous gas and abdominal X-ray report, names the diagnosis and differentials, and outlines resuscitation, surgical discussion, transfer and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute colicky abdominal pain with vomiting and obstipation: recognising and managing adhesive small bowel obstruction in a rural ED

stations.title: Colicky abdominal pain and vomiting in a 58-year-old woman
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 58-year-old woman in the ED with colicky periumbilical pain, worsening vomiting, absolute constipation and a previous laparoscopic operation. The candidate then interprets her observations, bloods, venous gas and CT report, names the diagnosis and differentials, and outlines the initial management, surgical referral and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute abdominal pain with vomiting: recognising and managing adhesive small bowel obstruction

stations.title: Collapse in the ED waiting area in a 75-year-old man
stations.desc: This station involves a witnessed collapse of a 75-year-old man in the ED waiting area. The candidate runs a rapid DRSABCD assessment and advanced life support for a shockable arrest. After return of spontaneous circulation, they do a primary survey and take a collateral history from his wife. They then interpret his observations, post-resuscitation 12-lead ECG and blood gas, name the cause and the reversible causes of cardiac arrest, and outline post-resuscitation care, emergency reperfusion and communication with his family.
stations.focus: In-hospital cardiac arrest: ANZCOR advanced life support for VF, finding the cause after ROSC, and post-resuscitation care with emergency PCI

stations.title: Consent for appendicectomy: a 38-year-old man on the surgical ward
stations.desc: This station involves a focused pre-operative history and examination of a 38-year-old carpenter admitted with right iliac fossa pain and booked for theatre tomorrow. The candidate then interprets his observations, admission bloods and CT report, recognises acute uncomplicated appendicitis and plans his preparation for theatre. They then explain the operation to him (nature, benefits, risks, alternatives, the consequences of no treatment and the day itself) to gain informed consent, and safety-net.
stations.focus: Pre-operative assessment and informed consent for laparoscopic appendicectomy (NBARCO)

stations.title: Consent for colonoscopy in a 25-year-old with chronic diarrhoea and weight loss
stations.desc: In this station the candidate sees a 25-year-old accountant in a hospital pre-admission clinic. His GP has referred him for colonoscopy after 2 years of intermittent diarrhoea, crampy abdominal pain, mouth ulcers and unintentional weight loss. The candidate takes a focused pre-procedure history, does a focused examination, then explains the colonoscopy and gains consent using IPBRAD (indication, procedure, benefits, risks, alternatives, documentation). In Part 2 the candidate interprets his pre-admission bloods, stool tests and the colonoscopy and histology report, recognises ileocolonic Crohn's disease, and plans induction treatment, staging, pre-immunosuppression screening and follow-up.
stations.focus: Explaining a colonoscopy and gaining informed consent, then interpreting the results of a suspected Crohn's disease work-up

stations.title: Constant right foot pain in a 62-year-old smoker
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and peripheral vascular examination of a 62-year-old woman in a rural ED with 3 weeks of constant right forefoot pain, then interpreting her observations, a bedside ankle-brachial index, bloods and a clinical photograph of the foot, and outlining escalation, transfer, analgesia and safety netting.
stations.focus: Recognising chronic limb-threatening ischaemia from the history and examination, and escalating it from a rural ED

stations.title: Constant right upper quadrant pain and vomiting after a rich dinner
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 41-year-old social worker in the ED with constant right upper quadrant pain since last night that radiates to the shoulder tip, with vomiting, fever and chills, and earlier milder episodes after rich meals. The candidate then interprets her observations, blood results (including a beta-hCG) and an upper abdominal ultrasound report, gives the diagnosis and differentials, outlines management in the ED, answers her fear that this is a tumour and safety-nets.
stations.focus: Acute right upper quadrant pain in a woman of reproductive age: diagnosing acute cholecystitis, excluding the dangerous differentials and managing it in the ED

stations.title: Constipation 8 days after a laparoscopic cholecystectomy in a 35-year-old tram driver
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of Wendy, a 35-year-old woman in general practice. She has not opened her bowels for 5 days, and her stools are hard, painful and leave blood on the paper. She had a laparoscopic cholecystectomy 8 days ago, went home on oxycodone without a laxative, takes oral iron and eats little fibre. The candidate then interprets her observations, blood tests and hospital discharge summary. They should recognise opioid-induced constipation (with iron, diet and reduced activity contributing) and an acute anal fissure, rule out postoperative obstruction and red flags for bowel cancer, and plan an analgesia review, laxatives, the iron plan, fissure care and safety netting.
stations.focus: Finding the cause of acute constipation (opioids and iron after surgery), excluding red flags and obstruction, and managing opioid-induced constipation in general practice

stations.title: Constipation and a change in bowel habit in a 62-year-old woman
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 62-year-old retired shop manager in general practice with 5 to 6 months of constipation, straining, tenesmus, fatigue and small amounts of blood mixed with her stool. Her brother was recently diagnosed with bowel cancer at 48, and she has come in hoping for a faecal occult blood test. The candidate then interprets her blood tests, recognises iron deficiency anaemia, treats suspected colorectal cancer as the leading diagnosis until it is excluded, explains why a screening FOBT is the wrong test, and arranges urgent colonoscopy and safety netting.
stations.focus: Picking up the red flags for colorectal cancer in a constipation history, and arranging urgent diagnostic colonoscopy instead of an FOBT

stations.title: Crushing chest pain at rest in a 66-year-old man with worsening angina
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 66-year-old retired painter with known angina who presents to the ED with 30 minutes of crushing central chest pain at rest that GTN has not relieved, after 3 weeks of worsening angina. The candidate then interprets his observations, 12-lead ECG, blood results and chest X-ray, makes a provisional diagnosis of unstable angina, risk stratifies him, and outlines ED management, secondary prevention and safety netting.
stations.focus: Recognising unstable (crescendo and rest) angina from the history, and knowing that a normal ECG and an early normal troponin do not exclude an acute coronary syndrome

stations.title: Difficulty swallowing in a 65-year-old retired chef
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 65-year-old retired chef in general practice with 3 months of progressive dysphagia to solids, weight loss and anorexia. She has long-standing reflux, takes naproxen regularly, is obese and is a heavy smoker. The candidate then interprets her blood tests, gastroscopy and biopsy report and staging CT, recognises a distal oesophageal adenocarcinoma arising in Barrett's oesophagus, and plans urgent specialist referral, nutrition support, how to tell her the news, and safety netting.
stations.focus: Telling oropharyngeal from oesophageal dysphagia and recognising the alarm features of oesophageal cancer in general practice

stations.title: Every morning at 7: one-sided headaches behind the left eye in a 30-year-old man in general practice
stations.desc: In this station the candidate takes a focused history from Abdul, a 30-year-old man in general practice, and does a focused neurological and head examination. He is in the middle of an attack of severe pain behind his left eye. The attacks have come almost every day for 2 months, wake him at about 7 am and last 2 to 3 hours. During them his left eye waters and his left nostril runs, and he cannot sit still. In Part 2 the candidate reads his observations, ECG and MRI brain, diagnoses cluster headache, and plans treatment for the attacks, prevention, neurology referral and safety netting, including his mood.
diagnosis: Cluster headache (left-sided, episodic, in a current bout)
stations.focus: Telling cluster headache apart from other primary and secondary headaches by its pattern and autonomic features, screening for red flags, and starting acute and preventive treatment in general practice

stations.title: Fatigue in a 23-year-old student: heavy periods and iron deficiency anaemia
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 23-year-old psychology student with 2 to 3 months of worsening fatigue in general practice. The candidate finds symptoms of anaemia and heavy menstrual bleeding and looks for the signs of iron deficiency. They then interpret her full blood count and film, iron studies and screening bloods, and plan iron replacement, treatment of the heavy bleeding, follow-up and safety netting.
stations.focus: Fatigue in a young woman: recognising iron deficiency anaemia from heavy menstrual bleeding, confirming it and managing both the cause and the iron deficit in general practice

stations.title: Fatigue in a 34-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes: an underactive thyroid and a macrocytic anaemia
stations.desc: This station involves a focused fatigue history and a thyroid-focused examination of a 34-year-old gardener and part-time paramedic student with type 1 diabetes. The candidate then interprets her full blood count, thyroid function tests and antibodies, inflammatory markers and electrolytes. They explain autoimmune hypothyroidism, start levothyroxine safely, plan the work-up of her macrocytic anaemia and safety-net in general practice.
stations.focus: Fatigue history in general practice: recognising autoimmune (Hashimoto) primary hypothyroidism with a macrocytic anaemia in a woman with type 1 diabetes, and starting thyroxine safely

stations.title: Fatigue, jaundice and a leg rash in a 63-year-old painter
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 63-year-old man who has had fatigue for several months. He is jaundiced and has a recurrent purpuric rash on his legs. The candidate then interprets his liver and blood tests and his hepatitis serology, recognises chronic hepatitis C with cirrhosis and probable cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis, and plans investigation, referral, treatment and safety netting in general practice.
stations.focus: Fatigue history that uncovers a blood-borne virus risk: recognising chronic hepatitis C with cirrhosis and extrahepatic vasculitis, and interpreting liver tests and hepatitis serology

stations.title: Fever, confusion and right arm weakness in a woman on methotrexate
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history, with collateral, and a neurological examination of a 68-year-old immunosuppressed woman brought in with fever, confusion, personality change and right arm weakness. In Part 2 the candidate interprets her observations, bloods, CT brain and CSF results, manages a central nervous system infection in the ED, and safety-nets with her partner.
stations.focus: Altered conscious state with fever: recognising, investigating and treating encephalitis in an immunosuppressed patient

stations.title: Five months of worsening breathlessness in a 72-year-old smoker with COPD
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 72-year-old man with COPD and a 50 pack-year smoking history, brought to the ED with 5 months of worsening breathlessness, weight loss, haemoptysis and a hoarse voice. The candidate then interprets his observations, ECG, bloods and chest X-ray, which shows a large right pleural effusion. They give a justified differential diagnosis, outline the pleural investigations and management, and safety-net.
stations.focus: Subacute breathlessness: eliciting the red flags for lung cancer, examining for and interpreting a large pleural effusion, and planning pleural fluid analysis and work-up

stations.title: Fresh rectal bleeding in a 75-year-old man: consent and rectal examination
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history from a 75-year-old accountant in the ED who passed painless dark red blood with clots a few hours ago, followed by consent for and a rectal examination. The candidate then interprets his observations, blood results and a colonoscopy report. They give the diagnosis and differentials, outline management in the emergency department, explain the findings to David and safety-net.
stations.focus: Acute painless rectal bleeding in an older man: consenting for and performing a rectal examination, risk-stratifying the bleed and recognising a diverticular bleed

stations.title: Generalised abdominal pain and fever in a man with untreated cirrhosis
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 45-year-old lawyer in the ED. He has had generalised abdominal pain and fever since yesterday, after two weeks of worsening abdominal swelling, jaundice, itch and bruising. He has alcohol-related cirrhosis with no follow-up and still drinks heavily. The candidate then interprets his observations, blood results and a diagnostic ascitic tap, gives the diagnosis and differentials, outlines emergency management, answers his questions about his liver and his work, and safety-nets.
context: Chronic liver disease lost to follow-up
diagnosis: Sepsis with presumed acute kidney injury
stations.focus: Fever and abdominal pain in decompensated cirrhosis: recognising and managing spontaneous bacterial peritonitis with sepsis

stations.title: He just collapsed: a witnessed in-hospital collapse in a 64-year-old man on a regional medical ward (Code Blue)
stations.desc: This station starts with a Code Blue on a medical ward in a regional hospital. The candidate is the first to arrive. Collin Barker, 64, was admitted last night with an NSTEMI and is waiting for transfer for coronary angiography. He collapsed while a third-year medical student was taking his history. In Part 1 the candidate runs basic life support (DRSABCD) on a manikin, with the examiner giving findings and asking questions: airway adjuncts and sizing a Guedel, CPR, and a safe shock when the AED advises one. Once the Code Blue team takes over, the candidate takes a focused collateral history from the student, the nurse and the chart, including his resuscitation status. In Part 2 the candidate interprets the defibrillator rhythm strip (ventricular fibrillation), a venous blood gas taken during CPR and his troponin and electrolyte results. They then hand over in ISBAR format, name the most likely cause and the reversible causes, outline advanced life support with drug timing and post-ROSC disposition, and contrast shockable with non-shockable rhythms.
stations.focus: Running DRSABCD for a witnessed in-hospital collapse, recognising VF and applying the ANZCOR adult ALS algorithm, including the reversible causes

stations.title: Heart health check: raised clinic blood pressure
stations.desc: This station involves a heart health check: a focused cardiovascular history and examination, then interpreting raised clinic blood pressure against home readings, the bloods and the ECG, counselling on diet and lifestyle, writing a three-month statin prescription and safety-netting.
stations.focus: Heart health check: cardiovascular prevention, hypertension, diet and prescribing

stations.title: High-chance NIPT result for a rare autosomal trisomy
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a pregnant woman referred after a high-chance NIPT result for a rare autosomal trisomy, then interpreting her NIPT, ultrasound and booking blood reports, explaining why the result is not diagnostic, advising on confirmatory testing, answering her question about a relative's failed NIPT and safety-netting.
diagnosis: Differential: true fetal rare autosomal trisomy vs confined placental mosaicism / false-positive NIPT result
stations.focus: Counselling after a high-risk NIPT result

stations.title: Horrible headache: recurrent one-sided headache with visual disturbance in a 24-year-old university student on the combined pill
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and a focused neurological examination of a 24-year-old university student in general practice. She has a severe, throbbing left-sided headache today, her fifth similar attack, each one preceded by visual disturbance. The candidate then interprets her observations and a urine pregnancy test, diagnoses migraine with aura, and explains a general practice management plan to her. The plan covers treatment of attacks, stopping the combined oral contraceptive pill because of the stroke risk, trigger management, prevention, study support and safety netting.
diagnosis: Combined oral contraceptive pill contraindicated (migraine with aura)
stations.focus: Taking a headache history that separates a primary from a dangerous secondary headache, diagnosing migraine with aura, and recognising that it rules out the combined oral contraceptive pill

stations.title: Infant with increased work of breathing
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history from the mother and a gentle examination of a 4-month-old with cough, fast breathing and poor feeding, then interpreting the observations, a reassessment on oxygen and a feeding trial, outlining oxygen, hydration with volumes for this infant and escalation, and safety-netting the mother.
stations.focus: Bronchiolitis in an infant with increased work of breathing

stations.title: Intermittent burning upper abdominal pain in a 45-year-old accountant
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 45-year-old man with 3 weeks of intermittent burning epigastric pain that comes after large meals and wakes him at night. He takes ibuprofen most days, smokes, is stressed at work and is worried about his heart. The candidate then interprets his ECG, blood tests and gastroscopy with biopsy, recognises a Helicobacter pylori duodenal ulcer with an NSAID contribution, and plans eradication therapy, NSAID withdrawal, confirmation of eradication and safety netting.
stations.focus: Dyspepsia in general practice: ALARM features, peptic ulcer risk factors, and managing an H. pylori ulcer

stations.title: Left iliac fossa pain, fever and a change in bowel habit in a 65-year-old teacher
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and abdominal examination of Andre, a 65-year-old teacher who has just been admitted to the general surgery ward. He has had 3 days of constant left iliac fossa pain with a change in bowel habit and a fever. The candidate then interprets his observations, bloods, urinalysis and CT report, gives the diagnosis and differentials, outlines ward management (including why colonoscopy is delayed), answers his fear of cancer and safety-nets.
stations.focus: Left iliac fossa pain with fever in an older adult: diagnosing acute uncomplicated diverticulitis, excluding complications and colorectal cancer, and managing it on the surgical ward

stations.title: Leg pain and a foot ulcer in a 75-year-old man with diabetes: peripheral vascular examination
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and peripheral vascular examination of the lower limbs in Daniel Clayton, a 75-year-old man with long-standing type 2 diabetes, high cholesterol and a heavy smoking history, who comes to his GP with left leg pain. In Part 2 the candidate interprets a wound assessment with a photograph, the ankle-brachial index and toe pressures, and blood results. They describe and diagnose an arterial ulcer with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia, then outline urgent vascular referral, wound care without elevation or compression, risk factor modification and safety netting.
stations.focus: Peripheral vascular examination of the lower limbs, then describing an arterial ulcer, interpreting the ABI and arranging management

stations.title: Legs that "just don't feel right" in a 28-year-old accountant
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and a lower limb neurological examination of a 28-year-old accountant in the ED. For 4 days she has had numbness and tingling spreading up her legs, and her legs are getting weaker. She also has urinary retention. In Part 2 the candidate interprets her observations, blood results and an MRI of the whole spine and brain. They place the lesion in the thoracic spinal cord, exclude cord compression, recognise an inflammatory demyelinating myelitis, and manage it in the ED with neurology. They then answer her questions about walking again and multiple sclerosis.
diagnosis: Acute transverse myelitis (lesion at T7-T8 vertebral level, T10 sensory level)
Second demyelinating event after probable right optic neuritis 2 years ago: likely relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (first presentation to medical care)
stations.focus: Lower limb neurological examination: separating upper from lower motor neuron signs, finding a sensory level, and treating a new myelopathy as an emergency until cord compression is excluded

stations.title: Lower abdominal pain in a 32-year-old teacher
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 32-year-old man in general practice with 12 hours of constant, dull periumbilical pain, nausea, vomiting, anorexia and fever, with pain on coughing and movement. The candidate then interprets a repeat set of observations and a urine dipstick, recognises probable acute appendicitis, arranges urgent hospital referral and answers his questions about the cause and complications.
stations.focus: Recognising early acute appendicitis in general practice and arranging urgent surgical referral

stations.title: Months of daytime sleepiness in a 48-year-old scientist
stations.desc: This station is a focused fatigue and sleep history, with a targeted examination, of Martha, a 48-year-old scientist seeing her GP. For several months she has felt sleepy and unrefreshed, and she is making errors at work. She snores heavily, drinks wine before bed and smokes, and she has hypertension and type 2 diabetes. In Part 2 the candidate interprets her sleep screening questionnaires and blood results. They should diagnose probable obstructive sleep apnoea, exclude the main differentials, arrange a sleep study, give driving advice and lifestyle measures, outline the treatment options and safety-net.
stations.focus: Fatigue: telling sleepiness from fatigue, screening the differentials with cluster questions and a sleep history, then recognising and working up obstructive sleep apnoea in general practice

stations.title: My arm keeps giving out: intermittent right arm weakness in a 63-year-old electrician in general practice
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and a structured neurological examination of the upper limbs in John Pascoe, a 63-year-old electrician seen in general practice. For 6 weeks his right arm has given out every now and then when he lifts or reaches overhead. He also has right neck pain that runs down his arm to his thumb. The candidate examines inspection, tone, power, reflexes and coordination, and screens for upper motor neuron signs. In Part 2 they interpret his observations, blood tests and MRI cervical spine report. They diagnose a right C5 and C6 radiculopathy from cervical spondylosis, contrast upper and lower motor neuron signs, and plan analgesia, physiotherapy, referral to a spinal surgeon and safety netting for spinal cord compression and stroke.
diagnosis: Cervical spondylosis with right foraminal stenosis
stations.focus: Performing a structured upper limb neurological examination, telling a lower motor neuron root lesion from an upper motor neuron one, and managing cervical radiculopathy in general practice

stations.title: Newly Diagnosed HIV: Explaining the Virus and ART
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a young man who has just been told he has HIV, then interpreting his confirmatory test, CD4 count, viral load and baseline results, and explaining how HIV affects the immune system and enters cells, what antiretroviral therapy can and cannot achieve, and what it means for his partner.
presentation: Patient questions about HIV and treatment
stations.focus: Newly diagnosed HIV: explaining the virus and what ART achieves

stations.title: Non-lactational breast abscess
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and breast examination of a woman who is not breastfeeding and has a red, painful breast lump that has not settled on antibiotics, then interpreting her bloods, ultrasound and mammogram, planning drainage, tissue diagnosis and referral, and explaining why cancer must be excluded.
stations.focus: Breast lump and breast abscess work-up

stations.title: Numb, painful feet in a 63-year-old man with type 2 diabetes
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and neurological and foot examination of a 63-year-old man with type 2 diabetes who has six months of symmetrical numbness and shooting pain in both feet and feels unsteady. The candidate then interprets his neuropathy bloods, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio and diabetes foot assessment, and plans glycaemic control, foot protection, falls prevention and safety netting.
diagnosis: Type 2 diabetes with poor glycaemic control
stations.focus: Altered sensation in the feet: recognising and working up diabetic peripheral neuropathy, and managing foot and falls risk in general practice

stations.title: Painful, deformed hands in a 41-year-old man on the rheumatology ward
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and a musculoskeletal hand examination of Jack Peralta, a 41-year-old café owner. He was admitted overnight to the rheumatology ward with a flare of painful, swollen hands, and his old notes cannot be found. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, his admission bloods and the only hand X-ray report on the system (from 2018). They then diagnose a flare of established seropositive, erosive rheumatoid arthritis after he stopped methotrexate, plan bridging treatment and the restart of a DMARD, and counsel him on methotrexate safety.
stations.focus: Systematic hand examination: recognising the deformities and synovitis of rheumatoid arthritis, telling it from other hand arthropathies, reading a rheumatoid hand X-ray and planning DMARD treatment safely

stations.title: Painful, stiff hands and wrists in a 35-year-old hairdresser in the rheumatology clinic
stations.desc: This station is a focused history and a rheumatological hand examination of Sarah Little, a 35-year-old hairdresser. Her GP has referred her to the rheumatology outpatient clinic with 3 months of pain and stiffness, worst in her hands and wrists. In Part 2 the candidate interprets her GP's blood results and an X-ray of her right hand and wrist, and diagnoses early seropositive, erosive rheumatoid arthritis. They then plan to start a DMARD safely in a woman who is planning another pregnancy, safety-net and arrange follow-up. They also explain which arthritides classically spare the DIP joints.
stations.focus: Systematic rheumatological hand examination: finding the symmetrical synovitis and DIP sparing of early rheumatoid arthritis, reading an early rheumatoid hand X-ray and starting methotrexate safely in a woman of child-bearing age

stations.title: Pale stools and a bleeding cord stump in a jaundiced 18-day-old
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history from the parent and a focused examination of an 18-day-old with prolonged jaundice, pale stools and an earlier cord-stump bleed after vitamin K was declined, then interpreting the observations, stool colour chart and antenatal and newborn records, arranging same-day urgent assessment with vitamin K by injection, and briefly counselling on the two-vessel cord, hips and safe sleep.
stations.focus: Newborn check and parent counselling: vitamin K, hips, jaundice, safe sleep

stations.title: Palpitations in a 66-year-old retired maintenance fitter
stations.desc: This station is a focused palpitations history and examination of Frank, a 66-year-old retired maintenance fitter seeing his GP. For a couple of months he has had episodes of fluttering that start and stop suddenly, and they now happen every day. He has hypertension and obstructive sleep apnoea, drinks about nine glasses of beer a day and smokes a pack a day. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, ECG and blood results, diagnoses paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, calculates his stroke risk, and outlines anticoagulation, rate control, investigations, risk factor management and safety netting.
stations.focus: Palpitations: characterising the rhythm, screening cardiac, endocrine and psychiatric causes and AF risk factors, then diagnosing paroxysmal AF and planning stroke prevention and risk factor management

stations.title: Persistent cough in a toddler not responding to treatment
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history from the parent and a focused examination of a toddler with a five-week cough that has not responded to antibiotics, steroids or bronchodilators, then interpreting the observations and a chest X-ray showing right lower lobe collapse, outlining urgent management of a likely inhaled foreign body with safety netting, and answering a question on retropharyngeal abscess.
stations.focus: Toddler with persistent cough and airway infection

stations.title: Pleuritic chest pain on day 5 after hip fracture surgery
stations.desc: This station involves a focused chest pain history and examination of a 47-year-old builder on the orthopaedic ward, day 5 after surgery for a right neck of femur fracture. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, ECG, bloods and CT pulmonary angiogram, starts management of a haemodynamically stable pulmonary embolism, explains it to him and safety-nets.
stations.focus: Postoperative pleuritic chest pain: a systems-based chest pain history, then recognising and managing pulmonary embolism

stations.title: Pre-biologic screening: an abnormal hepatitis B result in Crohn's disease
stations.desc: This station involves a focused pre-immunosuppression history and examination of a young man with a Crohn's disease flare, then interpreting his pre-biologic screening results (hepatitis B serology, TB and other screening, liver tests and faecal calprotectin), and explaining what a positive hepatitis B result means for his treatment, his liver and his partner.
stations.focus: Counselling before starting advanced therapy for IBD

stations.title: Pre-travel consultation: vaccines and travel health
stations.desc: This station involves a focused pre-travel history and a check that a young woman planning a long rural trip through mainland South-East Asia is fit for vaccination, then interpreting her immunisation record and itinerary, recommending and scheduling vaccines, advising on malaria, food and water, and safety-netting for during and after travel.
stations.focus: Pre-travel consultation: vaccines and travel health

stations.title: Pressure on top of my head: daily headache with neck stiffness in a 26-year-old PhD student in general practice
stations.desc: This station involves a focused headache history and a focused neurological, head and neck examination of James, a 26-year-old PhD student seen in general practice. For the past 6 weeks he has had a daily pressing headache that builds through the day, with neck and shoulder stiffness, while he writes his thesis. The candidate screens for red flags and features of other headache types, and finds that he takes analgesics most days. They then interpret his observations and a K10 questionnaire, diagnose tension-type headache, explain why no investigations are needed, and plan simple analgesia with limits to prevent medication-overuse headache, posture and lifestyle measures, stress support, smoking cessation, follow-up and safety netting.
diagnosis: Tension-type headache, currently daily for 6 weeks (on a background of occasional episodic TTH; at risk of chronic TTH, which needs ≥15 days/month for >3 months)
Psychological distress from thesis stress; smoking
stations.focus: Taking a structured headache history that screens for red flags, diagnosing tension-type headache and managing it without overusing analgesics

stations.title: Primary postpartum haemorrhage on delivery suite
stations.desc: This station involves a rapid focused history and examination of a woman bleeding heavily after birth, then interpreting her observations and blood results, leading the resuscitation and escalation of a primary postpartum haemorrhage from uterine atony, and explaining the plan, disposition and safety netting to her.
stations.focus: Primary postpartum haemorrhage

stations.title: Productive cough and fever four days after hospital discharge
stations.desc: This station is a focused acute cough history and respiratory examination of a 68-year-old retired teacher in general practice. Four days ago he was discharged from hospital after investigations for chest pain. He now has 2 days of cough with offensive yellow sputum, high fevers, breathlessness and right pleuritic chest pain. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, chest X-ray and bloods (including a D-dimer). They recognise right lower lobe pneumonia acquired around his hospital stay, exclude pulmonary embolism, score severity with CURB-65, arrange admission, answer his COVID worry and safety-net.
stations.focus: Acute productive cough after a recent hospital stay: a history that separates pneumonia from PE and heart failure, then interpreting results, scoring severity and deciding on admission

stations.title: Progressive dry cough and weight loss in a retired builder
stations.desc: This station is a focused chronic cough history and respiratory examination of a 75-year-old retired builder in general practice. He has months of dry cough, exertional breathlessness, weight loss, hoarseness and a dull upper chest pain, and was exposed to asbestos in the late 1960s and 1970s. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, chest X-ray and bloods, recognises a right apical lung mass suspicious for lung cancer, arranges an urgent CT and specialist referral, explains the result honestly and safety-nets.
stations.focus: Chronic cough: a red-flag and occupational history, then recognising and urgently referring a suspicious apical lung mass

stations.title: Projectile vomiting in a 5-week-old infant
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history from the mother and an examination of a 5-week-old boy with worsening vomiting after feeds, then interpreting his observations, venous gas and ultrasound, outlining fluid resuscitation and the plan for surgery, and safety-netting the mother.
stations.focus: Pyloric stenosis: a vomiting infant, dehydration and the metabolic alkalosis

stations.title: Prostate biopsy result: grading and staging
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a man whose prostate biopsy has shown cancer, then interpreting his PSA, MRI and biopsy results with him, explaining the Gleason score and ISUP Grade Group, outlining staging with PSMA PET/CT and the treatment pathway, and safety-netting.
stations.focus: Counselling a man with a raised PSA: biopsy, Gleason/ISUP grading and staging

stations.title: Racing heart in a 24-year-old teacher
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 24-year-old woman in the ED with 30 minutes of sudden, fast, regular palpitations. The candidate then interprets her observations, 12-lead ECG and blood results (including thyroid function), recognises a supraventricular tachycardia with untreated hyperthyroidism (probable Graves' disease), and outlines management and safety netting.
stations.focus: Palpitations: a focused history across systems, recognising SVT on the ECG, managing stable SVT and finding the thyrotoxic trigger

stations.title: Rectal pain in a 39-year-old barista
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 39-year-old barista in general practice with 4 days of severe anal pain that starts with each bowel motion, a small amount of bright red bleeding, and a background of constipation and hard stools. The candidate must ask about sensitive matters tactfully, rule out the other perianal causes, and gain consent for a perianal examination with a chaperone. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations and the perianal examination record and photograph. They must recognise an acute posterior midline anal fissure with no sentinel tag, and a separate long-standing skin tag that is incidental. They then plan conservative management, a sphincter relaxant if needed, safety netting and review.
stations.focus: Anal pain on defecation: a focused, sensitive history, a perianal examination with consent, and general practice management of an anal fissure

stations.title: Reduced movements and worry after a previous stillbirth
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a woman at 36 weeks with reduced fetal movements after a previous stillbirth, then interpreting her observations and CTG, explaining honestly what a normal trace means, planning further assessment, answering her questions about aspirin, food safety and later health, and safety-netting.
diagnosis: Reduced fetal movements with normal cardiotocograph
stations.focus: Antenatal visit: food advice, reduced fetal movements, anxiety after stillbirth and later health risks

stations.title: Right temporal headache and blurred vision in a 64-year-old man
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 64-year-old man in the ED with 16 hours of right temporal headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication and a blurred right eye. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, which show worsening vision while every vital sign stays in the white zone, and his blood results. They then manage giant cell arteritis with visual involvement as a sight-threatening emergency and explain the diagnosis, treatment and red flags to the patient.
stations.focus: New headache over 50: recognising giant cell arteritis with visual involvement and starting high-dose corticosteroids without delay

stations.title: Right upper quadrant pain with vomiting in an older woman
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and abdominal examination of an older woman with right upper quadrant pain, vomiting and distension, then interpreting her bloods, ECG and abdominal X-ray, explaining why this is gallstone ileus and not cholecystitis or cholangitis, and outlining management, counselling and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute right upper quadrant pain with suspected cholecystitis, cholangitis or gallstone ileus

stations.title: Right upper quadrant pain, abdominal swelling and vomiting blood
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 62-year-old man with right upper quadrant pain, abdominal swelling and haematemesis after 15 years of heavy drinking that has escalated in the month since his wife died. The candidate then interprets his repeat observations, bloods and abdominal ultrasound, gives the diagnosis and differentials, and outlines emergency management, an explanation to the patient and safety netting.
stations.focus: Haematemesis in a heavy drinker: recognising decompensated alcohol-related liver disease and managing a suspected variceal bleed

stations.title: Right upper quadrant pain, fever and yellow skin in a 28-year-old teacher
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 28-year-old school teacher in a rural ED. She has had fevers since last night and 2 hours of severe crampy right upper quadrant pain, her husband has noticed yellow skin, and she has rigors, pale stools, dark urine and itch. The candidate then interprets her observations, blood results with a venous gas and an upper abdominal ultrasound report. They give the diagnosis and differentials, outline sepsis management and the need for biliary drainage in a rural setting, answer her questions and safety-net.
stations.focus: Jaundice with right upper quadrant pain and fever: recognising acute cholangitis (Charcot's triad), separating obstructive from hepatic jaundice and starting sepsis management with urgent biliary drainage

stations.title: Right upper quadrant pain, itch and dark urine in a 40-year-old man
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a frustrated 40-year-old man in the ED with about 10 days of a viral-type prodrome (fever, joint aches, an itchy urticarial rash and malaise), dark urine and pale stools for a week, right upper quadrant pain for 3 days and yellow eyes today. He recently shared needles. The candidate then interprets his observations, liver function and other bloods, hepatitis serology and an abdominal ultrasound report, names the diagnosis and differentials, and outlines management, public health actions, harm reduction and safety netting.
diagnosis: Icteric phase of acute viral hepatitis
stations.focus: Jaundice with right upper quadrant pain: taking a hepatitis risk history, reading a hepatitic LFT pattern and hepatitis B serology, and managing acute hepatitis B

stations.title: Severe abdominal pain after curettage for abnormal bleeding
stations.desc: This station involves assessing and resuscitating a woman who deteriorates in day-surgery recovery after a hysteroscopy and D&C, then interpreting her reassessment, blood gas, ECG, operation record and pre-operative ultrasound, recognising uterine perforation, escalating, placing her original bleeding in PALM-COEIN and explaining why obesity raises endometrial cancer risk.
stations.focus: Abnormal uterine bleeding assessment

stations.title: Severe epigastric pain going through to the back in a 56-year-old builder
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 56-year-old builder in the ED. He woke with severe epigastric pain going through to his back after a night of heavy drinking. The candidate then interprets his observations, bloods and venous gas, ECG and abdominal ultrasound report. They give the diagnosis and differentials, outline management in the emergency department, answer his worry about cancer and set escalation triggers.
stations.focus: Acute epigastric pain radiating to the back: diagnosing alcohol-related acute pancreatitis, finding its cause and grading its severity, and starting early management

stations.title: Severe headache, fever and neck stiffness in an 18-year-old student
stations.desc: This station involves a time-critical focused history and examination of an 18-year-old unvaccinated student brought to the ED by ambulance with a 4-hour severe headache, fever, photophobia and neck stiffness. In Part 2 the candidate interprets her observations, bloods and CSF results, diagnoses pneumococcal bacterial meningitis, manages it in the ED according to eTG, and answers her questions about migraine and whether her family can catch it.
stations.focus: Acute headache with fever: separating meningitis from other causes of headache, starting treatment without delay, and interpreting the CSF

stations.title: Sharp, positional chest pain in a 34-year-old software engineer
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 34-year-old woman in the ED late at night with sharp pleuritic chest pain that is worse lying down and better sitting forward. The candidate then interprets her observations, ECG, bloods and chest X-ray, gives a differential that covers the life-threatening cardiac, pulmonary and oesophageal causes, and outlines management and safety netting.
context: Young adult with no cardiovascular risk factors
stations.focus: Acute chest pain in a young adult: recognising acute pericarditis on history, examination and ECG while excluding its life-threatening mimics

stations.title: Simple febrile seizure
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history from the parent and an examination of a toddler who has had a first seizure with fever, then interpreting the observations and a reassessment, classifying the seizure, deciding on investigations, and counselling the parent on recurrence, seizure first aid, discharge and when to return.
stations.focus: A simple febrile seizure: assessment, the parents' questions, discharge and first aid

stations.title: Six-week cough in a young woman
stations.desc: This station involves a focused cough history and examination of Jenny Sok, a 26-year-old law student who was born in Cambodia and has had a worsening productive cough for 6 weeks. In Part 2 the candidate interprets her observations, blood results and chest X-ray, gives the most likely diagnosis, and plans investigation, urgent referral and safety netting in general practice.
stations.focus: Chronic productive cough with haemoptysis: a structured cough history with differential clusters and risk factors, then recognising and starting the work-up of suspected pulmonary tuberculosis

stations.title: Sudden aggression in a boy with intellectual disability
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history from the parent of a 10-year-old boy with intellectual disability and a recent change in behaviour, and a focused examination, then interpreting his observations, bedside tests and a teacher-completed Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire, and outlining management and safety netting.
stations.focus: Child with intellectual disability and behavioural change

stations.title: Sudden breathlessness in a 23-year-old man playing soccer
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 23-year-old engineering student who comes to the ED with sudden breathlessness and left-sided pleuritic chest pain that started during social soccer. The candidate then interprets his observations, ECG and chest X-ray, which shows a large left pneumothorax with no tension. They give a justified differential diagnosis, outline ED management of a symptomatic primary spontaneous pneumothorax, and safety-net, including advice on recurrence, smoking, flying and diving.
stations.focus: Acute breathlessness in a young adult: eliciting the features and risk factors of a primary spontaneous pneumothorax, excluding tension and the dangerous differentials, reading the chest X-ray, and managing a symptomatic pneumothorax

stations.title: Sudden breathlessness in a 70-year-old man with previous bypass surgery
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 70-year-old retired nurse brought to the ED by ambulance with sudden severe breathlessness after a month of worsening fatigue, orthopnoea and leg swelling. The candidate then interprets his observations, ECG, bloods with a venous gas and a chest X-ray, diagnoses acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema on a background of heart failure, weighs the differentials (ACS, malignant effusion, infection, PE) and outlines ED management and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute breathlessness: eliciting heart failure symptoms, excluding the dangerous differentials, reading a chest X-ray of pulmonary oedema with effusions, and managing acute pulmonary oedema in the ED

stations.title: Sudden breathlessness while jogging in a 20-year-old student
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 20-year-old law student brought to the ED by ambulance. She became suddenly short of breath an hour ago while jogging, after forgetting to take her reliever. The candidate first has to recognise how severe the attack is and start treatment. They then take a targeted history covering triggers, asthma risk and the dangerous differentials, and examine her. In Part 2 they interpret her observations, an arterial blood gas taken on oxygen and an ECG. They diagnose a severe acute asthma exacerbation, give a justified list of differentials, outline ED management under the Australian Asthma Handbook and safety-net for discharge.
stations.focus: Acute dyspnoea in a young adult with known asthma: judging severity and starting treatment early, screening the dangerous differentials, interpreting an acute respiratory alkalosis, and managing a severe asthma exacerbation

stations.title: Sudden hearing loss in one ear on waking
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and ear and neurological examination of a woman with sudden hearing loss in one ear, then interpreting her audiogram, tympanometry and recent bloods, and explaining the urgent management: same-day ENT contact, prompt steroids with a diabetes plan, an MRI to exclude a retrocochlear lesion, and safety netting.
stations.focus: Sudden hearing loss

stations.title: Sudden left leg weakness in a man with atrial fibrillation
stations.desc: This station involves a time-critical focused history and neurological examination of a 65-year-old man with sudden weakness and numbness of the left leg and urinary incontinence after two earlier brief episodes. The candidate then interprets his observations, bloods, ECG and code stroke CT, separates stroke from TIA, localises the lesion to the anterior cerebral artery territory, works through reperfusion while he is taking apixaban, and gives secondary prevention and safety netting.
diagnosis: Acute ischaemic stroke, right anterior cerebral artery territory
stations.focus: Acute focal weakness: recognising stroke, localising an anterior cerebral artery syndrome and deciding on reperfusion in a patient on apixaban

stations.title: Sudden painful finger overnight in a 36-year-old fisherman
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 36-year-old fisherman in the ED. He woke overnight with a hot, swollen, exquisitely tender left ring finger DIP joint, and had a self-limiting big toe attack last year. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, bloods, joint aspirate and hand X-ray. They then diagnose acute gout while keeping septic arthritis in view, manage the flare, and counsel him on preventing further attacks, red flags and follow-up.
stations.focus: Acute monoarthritis: diagnosing recurrent gout, excluding septic arthritis, treating the flare and planning prevention

stations.title: Sudden pleuritic chest pain after a long-haul flight
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 51-year-old woman in a metropolitan ED with sudden, sharp chest pain that woke her, breathlessness and a swollen right leg. The candidate then interprets her observations, ECG, bloods and CT pulmonary angiogram, justifies the diagnosis of pulmonary embolism from her risk factors, and outlines management and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute pleuritic chest pain: eliciting VTE risk factors, excluding the red-flag differentials, and confirming and managing pulmonary embolism

stations.title: Sudden right upper quadrant pain after a barbecue lunch
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and abdominal examination of a 47-year-old teacher with sudden right upper quadrant pain after a fatty meal, then interpreting her observations, bloods with a cholestatic liver function pattern and an ultrasound report, giving the diagnosis and differentials, outlining management in the emergency department, explaining the risk factors for gallstones and safety-netting.
stations.focus: Acute right upper quadrant pain: telling acute cholecystitis apart from the rest of gallstone disease and reading a cholestatic LFT pattern

stations.title: Sudden tearing chest pain and a blackout in a 66-year-old man
stations.desc: This station involves a focused chest pain history and examination of a 66-year-old man brought to the ED by ambulance with sudden, tearing central chest pain through to his back, a brief blackout and breathlessness. He becomes hypotensive during the station. The candidate then interprets his observations, ECG, bloods and CT aortogram, recognises a Stanford type A aortic dissection, and outlines emergency management and safety netting.
stations.focus: Acute chest pain: a cluster-question history that recognises aortic dissection, a bedside search for its signs, and emergency surgical management without antithrombotics

stations.title: Sudden wheeze and chest tightness in a 35-year-old man with asthma
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of Jeff, a 35-year-old accountant with lifelong asthma. He comes to the ED with breathlessness, chest tightness and wheeze that started an hour ago after exposure to cat fur and pollen. He cannot finish sentences and is using his accessory muscles. The candidate then interprets his observations, bloods with a venous gas and a chest X-ray, and grades the attack as severe acute asthma. They justify the diagnosis against anaphylaxis, pneumothorax, PE, MI, pneumonia and COPD, outline ED management to the Australian Asthma Handbook, and safety-net with an action plan, a preventer and follow-up.
stations.focus: Acute breathlessness with wheeze: taking a targeted asthma history while treating, screening the dangerous differentials and red flags, grading severity, and managing severe acute asthma in the ED

stations.title: Sudden worst-ever headache while jogging in a 40-year-old man with polycystic kidney disease
