stations.desc: This station involves a time-critical focused history and examination of a 40-year-old actuary with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) and hypertension. He has a thunderclap headache that began while jogging, had a warning headache 2 weeks ago, and now has reduced GCS, meningism and subhyaloid (Terson) haemorrhages. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, which show him getting worse, his bloods and his CT brain with CT angiogram. They diagnose aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage with early hydrocephalus, manage it in the ED, and explain how to recognise raised intracranial pressure with impending coning.
diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (ruptured anterior communicating artery aneurysm)
Acute hydrocephalus with raised intracranial pressure
stations.focus: Thunderclap headache: recognising subarachnoid haemorrhage, choosing the right first investigation, and recognising raised intracranial pressure with impending coning

stations.title: Ten days of cough with rusty sputum in a 60-year-old teacher
stations.desc: This station involves a focused cough history and respiratory examination of a 60-year-old teacher seeing her GP. In Part 2 the candidate interprets her observations, blood results and chest X-ray report, diagnoses left lower lobe community-acquired pneumonia with a small parapneumonic effusion, assesses severity with CURB-65, plans outpatient treatment, answers her fear of cancer and safety-nets.
stations.focus: Productive cough after a viral illness: a systems-based cough history and chest examination, then chest X-ray interpretation, severity assessment and outpatient management of community-acquired pneumonia

stations.title: The worst headache behind my left eye: recurrent unilateral headache with aura in a 32-year-old woman in general practice
stations.desc: This station involves a focused headache history and a focused neurological examination of Sara, a 32-year-old accountant seen in general practice. She has a 14-hour throbbing left-sided headache that followed a visual and sensory aura, and she has had several similar attacks recently while under stress. The candidate then interprets her observations, a urine pregnancy test and her own headache record. They diagnose migraine with aura, make and explain an imaging decision, treat the current attack, stop the combined pill, and plan trigger management, smoking cessation, possible prevention and safety netting.
diagnosis: Combined oral contraceptive contraindicated (migraine with aura)
Smoking and alcohol increased by stress
stations.focus: Taking a structured headache history that screens for red flags, diagnosing migraine with aura, and recognising that the combined pill is contraindicated

stations.title: Three days of worsening breathlessness in a 67-year-old man with heart failure
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 67-year-old man with known heart failure and atrial fibrillation who comes to the ED with 3 days of worsening exertional breathlessness, orthopnoea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea and ankle swelling. The candidate then interprets his observations, ECG, bloods and chest X-ray. They diagnose acute decompensated heart failure, identify a recent course of over-the-counter ibuprofen as the likely precipitant (with an acute kidney injury), weigh the differentials, outline ED management and safety-net for discharge.
context: Known heart failure and atrial fibrillation
stations.focus: Worsening breathlessness in known heart failure: eliciting congestion and the precipitants of decompensation, reading the chest X-ray and bloods, and managing acute decompensated heart failure in the ED

stations.title: Three hours of worsening breathlessness a month after a heart attack
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of Sam Stevens, a 73-year-old man in a metropolitan ED with 2 weeks of worsening breathlessness that became much worse over the last 3 hours. He had a heart attack a month ago, has poorly controlled hypertension and has been taking a lot of over-the-counter ibuprofen for back pain. The candidate then interprets his observations, ECG, bloods with a venous gas and chest X-ray, diagnoses acute pulmonary oedema from heart failure brought on by the recent MI and the NSAID use, outlines ED management and safety-nets.
diagnosis: Congestive heart failure after recent myocardial infarction
stations.focus: Acute breathlessness after a recent MI: eliciting heart failure symptoms and the NSAID precipitant, reading a chest X-ray of pulmonary oedema systematically, and managing acute pulmonary oedema in the ED

stations.title: Thyroid examination in a 32-year-old woman with a neck swelling
stations.desc: This station involves a short focused history and a full thyroid examination of a 32-year-old accountant who has a neck swelling, weight loss and an irregular pulse. The candidate then interprets her thyroid function tests and antibodies, ECG and baseline bloods, makes the diagnosis, and plans rate control, antithyroid treatment, anticoagulation assessment, referrals and safety netting in general practice.
stations.focus: Systematic thyroid status and goitre examination: recognising Graves' disease with orbitopathy and thyrotoxic atrial fibrillation, and starting safe management in general practice

stations.title: Tired, thirsty and up at night: fatigue in a 33-year-old mechanic
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 33-year-old mechanic with 5 months of fatigue, thirst and nocturia. The candidate then interprets his urine dipstick, fasting bloods and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, makes a new diagnosis of type 2 diabetes, and plans initial management and safety netting in general practice.
stations.focus: Fatigue in a young adult: a broad screening history that finds the osmotic symptoms, then diagnosing and starting management of type 2 diabetes in general practice

stations.title: Tiredness, steatorrhoea and an itchy rash on the knees in a 28-year-old lawyer
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 28-year-old lawyer with two months of tiredness, abdominal pain, pale foul-smelling diarrhoea, weight loss and an itchy rash on both knees. The candidate then interprets a photograph of the rash and her blood and stool results, and plans the coeliac disease work-up and management, safety netting and follow-up in general practice.
stations.focus: Fatigue with malabsorption: recognising coeliac disease with dermatitis herpetiformis and iron deficiency, interpreting coeliac serology, and keeping the patient on gluten until biopsy in general practice

stations.title: Toddler with stridor: croup
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history from the mother and a gentle examination of a 2-year-old with a barking cough and stridor, then interpreting the observations on arrival and on reassessment, classifying the croup, outlining management with weight-based doses, and safety-netting the mother.
stations.focus: Croup in a toddler with stridor

stations.title: Turner syndrome: short stature and delayed puberty
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history from the mother and a focused examination of a 13-year-old girl with short stature and absent puberty, then interpreting her growth chart, karyotype, blood tests, echocardiogram, renal ultrasound and audiology, explaining Turner syndrome and the management plan to the mother, and safety-netting.
stations.focus: Turner syndrome: short stature and delayed puberty in a girl

stations.title: Two days of headache, fever and neck stiffness in a 32-year-old teacher on prednisolone
stations.desc: This station has a focused history and examination of a 32-year-old high school teacher in the ED. He has had 2 days of a worsening generalised headache with fever, neck stiffness, vomiting, photophobia and phonophobia after a recent viral illness. He has been taking prednisolone since an asthma admission last month and has a penicillin allergy. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his observations, bloods, CT brain report and CSF results. They then manage bacterial meningitis in an immunosuppressed patient according to eTG, including Listeria cover that takes his allergy into account and steroid cover. Finally they answer his questions about COVID and whether his girlfriend can catch it.
stations.focus: Headache with fever and meningism in an immunosuppressed patient: recognising bacterial meningitis, treating without delay and adjusting empirical therapy for corticosteroid use and penicillin allergy

stations.title: Two months of abdominal discomfort and an erratic bowel habit in a 26-year-old IT analyst
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 26-year-old IT analyst in general practice with 2 months of vague, intermittent lower abdominal discomfort, bloating and alternating diarrhoea and constipation. She had food poisoning 6 months ago, her job is stressful, she drinks milk-based bubble tea, and she is worried about bowel cancer. The candidate then reads her bloods, coeliac serology, faecal calprotectin and stool tests, all normal, makes a working diagnosis of irritable bowel syndrome (mixed type, possibly post-infectious), explains it positively and plans first-line management with clear safety netting.
stations.focus: Chronic lower GI symptoms in a young adult: screening for red flags, ruling out organic disease with first-line tests, and making and explaining a positive diagnosis of IBS

stations.title: Two months of left iliac fossa pain and bloody diarrhoea in a 25-year-old man
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 25-year-old accountant in general practice with 2 months of left iliac fossa pain, diarrhoea with blood and mucus, weight loss and tender lumps on his shins. The candidate then interprets his blood tests, stool tests and colonoscopy with biopsy report, recognises ulcerative colitis (proctosigmoiditis) that is not acute severe, plans first-line management with the gastroenterologist, and explains the complications and extraintestinal manifestations.
stations.focus: Recognising and confirming inflammatory bowel disease in a young adult with chronic bloody diarrhoea, and distinguishing ulcerative colitis from Crohn's disease

stations.title: Two months of right iliac fossa pain and loose stools in a 20-year-old university student
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 20-year-old engineering student with 2 months of right iliac fossa pain, loose stools with blood mixed in that wake her at night, mild fevers and unintentional weight loss. She is a social smoker and has recently been taking aspirin. On examination she has right iliac fossa tenderness, perianal inflammation with skin tags and mild finger clubbing. The candidate then interprets her blood, stool and urine results and her colonoscopy and biopsy report, recognises ileocolonic Crohn's disease with perianal disease and iron deficiency anaemia, and plans shared care with gastroenterology, lifestyle changes and safety netting.
stations.focus: Chronic right iliac fossa pain and diarrhoea in a young woman: recognising and managing Crohn's disease

stations.title: Unwell newborn with suspected early-onset sepsis
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history from the midwife and mother and an A to E examination of a 14-hour-old term baby who has become unwell, then interpreting the reassessment, blood gas, blood count, CRP and chest X-ray, outlining the management of early-onset sepsis with shock with doses for this baby, and safety-netting the family.
stations.focus: Suspected early-onset neonatal sepsis

stations.title: Vomiting blood and black stools in a 74-year-old man on ibuprofen and aspirin
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 74-year-old retired sandal maker brought to the ED by ambulance. He has had black, tarry stools for 2 weeks and today vomited blood twice after his usual epigastric pain suddenly got worse. He takes ibuprofen and aspirin. The candidate then interprets his observations, bloods and venous gas and an erect chest X-ray report. They calculate a Glasgow-Blatchford score, give the diagnosis and differentials, outline resuscitation and initial ED management of an upper GI bleed, answer his questions about the cause and his tablets, and set escalation triggers.
diagnosis: Bleeding peptic ulcer (NSAID and aspirin related)
stations.focus: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding: recognising a compensated haemorrhage, resuscitating, risk stratifying with the Glasgow-Blatchford score, and starting non-variceal management with early endoscopy

stations.title: Woke up extremely breathless: a 75-year-old smoker with COPD
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 75-year-old retired plumber with COPD. He was brought to the ED by ambulance after waking extremely breathless, with wheeze and a new yellow cough. The candidate then interprets his observations, arterial blood gas, bloods and chest X-ray. They diagnose an infective exacerbation of COPD with compensated hypercapnia, weigh the differentials (pneumonia, pneumothorax, PE, cardiac causes and lung cancer), outline ED management with controlled oxygen, and safety-net for discharge.
stations.focus: Acute breathlessness in an older smoker with COPD: eliciting the features of an infective exacerbation, excluding the dangerous differentials, reading the blood gas and chest X-ray, and managing the exacerbation with controlled oxygen

stations.title: Worsening breathlessness and cough in a 51-year-old retired chef on home oxygen
stations.desc: A focused dyspnoea history and respiratory examination of Nancy Perk, a 51-year-old retired chef with COPD on home oxygen, seen in general practice. Over the past week her breathlessness has worsened and her chronic cough has become more frequent, with foul, purulent sputum and fever, two weeks after she visited her sister in hospital. In Part 2 the candidate interprets her observations, ECG, chest X-ray report, bloods and respiratory virus swab, and diagnoses an infective acute exacerbation of COPD. They exclude the mimics, arrange ambulance transfer with controlled oxygen, bronchodilators, prednisolone and an antibiotic suited to her penicillin allergy, answer her COVID worry and safety-net.
stations.focus: Dyspnoea in known COPD: a history that covers the cardinal exacerbation symptoms, cluster questions for at least six differentials and a COPD examination, then recognising an infective exacerbation, excluding its mimics, and starting safe treatment

stations.title: Worsening breathlessness in a 74-year-old retired meteorologist
stations.desc: This station is a focused breathlessness history and cardiorespiratory examination of Adam Jung, a 74-year-old retired meteorologist seeing his GP. His breathlessness has worsened over years and is now brought on by walking 10 m. He has orthopnoea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, exertional chest tightness and exertional dizziness with a brief blackout. In Part 2 the candidate interprets his ECG, chest X-ray report, blood results and echocardiogram report. They should classify him as NYHA class IV and diagnose heart failure with preserved ejection fraction caused by severe calcific aortic stenosis. They then arrange hospital care and heart team assessment for aortic valve replacement, explain the problem to Adam and safety-net.
diagnosis: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
stations.focus: Dyspnoea: measuring breathlessness by what the patient can do, screening across systems with cluster questions and asking for the aortic stenosis triad, then recognising severe symptomatic aortic stenosis with HFpEF on the echo and planning valve replacement

stations.title: Worsening breathlessness in a 78-year-old retired biologist
stations.desc: This station is a focused breathlessness history and cardiorespiratory examination of Kathy Jefferson, a 78-year-old retired biologist seeing her GP. She has 2 months of breathlessness that has got much worse over the past week, with orthopnoea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, and she had an NSTEMI 6 months ago. In Part 2 the candidate interprets her observations, ECG, chest X-ray report and blood results. They should diagnose new decompensated congestive heart failure (NYHA class IV) with pulmonary oedema and bilateral pleural effusions, arrange transfer to hospital, explain heart failure to her and safety-net.
stations.focus: Dyspnoea: quantifying breathlessness by exercise tolerance and screening other systems with cluster questions, then recognising decompensated congestive heart failure on the chest X-ray, ECG and bloods, and arranging hospital care

stations.title: Worsening headache after a fall in a 72-year-old man on apixaban
stations.desc: The candidate is a junior doctor in a rural ED. Harold Brennan, 72, has had three days of a slowly worsening headache. They take a focused history, which brings out a minor fall five days earlier in which he hit the right side of his head, and the fact that he takes apixaban. They then do a focused examination. In Part 2 they interpret his observations, which show early neurological deterioration, his bloods and a non-contrast CT brain. They diagnose a right subdural haematoma with midline shift, reverse the anticoagulant, arrange urgent neurosurgical referral and retrieval, address the cause of the fall, and answer his fear that he has a brain tumour.
diagnosis: Right subdural haematoma with midline shift
stations.focus: Recognising a subdural haematoma after minor head trauma in an anticoagulated older adult: the history, interpreting the CT, reversing the anticoagulant and getting him to neurosurgery

stations.title: Yellow eyes in a 23-year-old returned traveller
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and gastrointestinal examination of a 23-year-old university student whose housemates noticed his eyes were yellow, a week after nausea, chills, anorexia and right upper quadrant discomfort. He came back 4 weeks ago from South East Asia, where he ate local food, drank heavily and had unprotected sex, and he does not know his vaccination status. The candidate then interprets his liver and blood tests, hepatitis serology and STI screen, recognises acute hepatitis A with preserved liver function, and plans supportive care, public health notification, management of contacts, hepatitis B vaccination, repeat HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B and C testing after the window period, and safety netting.
stations.focus: Approach to jaundice in a returned traveller: history of risk factors, a GI examination with few signs, LFT patterns, hepatitis serology and public health management

stations.title: Yellow eyes in a 30-year-old woman back from Thailand
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination of a 30-year-old interior designer in general practice. Her partner noticed yesterday that her eyes look yellow. She has had two weeks of feeling hot, poor appetite, malaise, right upper quadrant pain, dark urine, pale stools, itch and nausea, and she came back from Thailand a month ago without any pre-travel vaccines. The candidate then interprets her hepatitis serology, liver function tests and abdominal ultrasound, recognises acute hepatitis A in a patient who is vaccine-immune to hepatitis B, and plans supportive care, public health notification, protection of her partner, monitoring and safety netting.
stations.focus: Jaundice in a returned traveller: the 4 Ps, hepatitis and travel risk factors, and reading hepatitis serology and liver tests

stations.title: Yellow eyes in a 78-year-old retired welder
stations.desc: This station involves a focused history and examination in general practice of a 78-year-old retired welder with more than a month of deepening jaundice, tea-coloured urine, pale stools, a mild epigastric ache radiating to the back, anorexia, weight loss and lethargy. He had a cholecystectomy 10 years ago, developed type 2 diabetes 3 years ago and has smoked since he was 15. He wonders whether his wife's carrot juice is to blame. The candidate then interprets his blood tests, tumour marker, hepatitis serology and a pancreatic-protocol CT, recognises obstructive jaundice from a suspected pancreatic head cancer, refers him urgently through the optimal care pathway, explains the results and gives safety-netting advice.
presentation: Epigastric pain radiating to the back
stations.focus: Recognising obstructive jaundice with red flags for pancreatic cancer in an older patient, and arranging urgent referral from general practice

stations.title: Yellow skin, abdominal pain and fever in a 56-year-old accountant
stations.desc: This station involves a focused jaundice history and examination of a 56-year-old woman in general practice. She has had 5 days of jaundice with right upper quadrant pain, fever, pale stools, itch, dizziness and new confusion, on a background of known untreated gallstones. The candidate then interprets her worsening observations, blood results, ultrasound and next-day ERCP report. They recognise severe acute cholangitis from common bile duct stones with sepsis, hypotension and hypoperfusion (at risk of septic shock), and plan sepsis resuscitation, urgent biliary drainage, cholecystectomy and safety netting.
diagnosis: Sepsis with hypotension (at risk of septic shock)
stations.focus: Taking a jaundice history that recognises Charcot's triad and confusion, and managing severe acute cholangitis from choledocholithiasis
